item.title: Kelly_RM: Kelly criterion experiments for trade sizing
item.description:
Kelly_RM

NotebooksKelly criterion
PythonJupyterbacktesting.pypandasNumPyhttpxAltairseaborn

Kelly_RM is an AlgoÉTS research repository about risk management with the Kelly criterion, the rule that sets a bet size from the probability of winning and the payoff ratio. Its root README is empty; the code pairs a coin-flip simulation of Kelly betting with a notebook that backtests an RSI strategy, measures win odds per ticker and turns them into a Kelly fraction. It suits readers who want to see how the formula behaves before applying it to a strategy.

item.title: LegosTracker: LEGO catalog data and set price history
item.description:
LegosTracker

Notebooks and data
PythonJupyterPlaywrightPydanticpandasscikit-learnMatplotlibBeautifulSoup

LegosTracker is an AlgoÉTS data project that looks at LEGO sets as a market: the Rebrickable catalog says which sets, parts and themes exist, and a BrickEconomy scraper adds the prices sets fetch over time. It is meant for collectors and data science readers who want to explore the catalog or test simple price models on one set. The article Economics of LEGO Sets with Data Science tells the story with charts.

item.title: MarkokChainMonteCarlo: Monte Carlo and Markov chain backtests
item.description:
MarkokChainMonteCarlo

NotebooksMonte Carlo
PythonJupyterbacktesting.pypandasNumPySciPyhttpxscikit-learn

MarkokChainMonteCarlo is an AlgoÉTS research repository that backtests investment strategies with stochastic price simulations. Its notebooks estimate Apple (AAPL) price paths with a forward Monte Carlo model and a Markov chain over price ranges, then use those simulations inside a backtesting.py strategy compared with buy and hold. The forward Monte Carlo part is explained step by step in Predicting Stock Prices with Monte Carlo Simulations.

item.title: PolyFEMBlenderPlugin: PolyFEM simulations from a Blender scene
item.description:
PolyFEMBlenderPlugin

Blender add-onDocker
PythonBlender 4.2PolyFEMTetWildmeshioGitHub Actions

PolyFEMBlenderPlugin is an experimental Blender extension that turns selected objects, materials and contact settings into a PolyFEM JSON setup and runs the finite-element simulation without leaving Blender. It was written for the ÉTS lab’s simulation work and is published under ETSim, for people who prepare scenes in Blender but solve them with PolyFEM.

Overview

polyfem/__init__.py registers one panel, the property groups and the operators. On registration it also installs meshio with pip into Blender’s user modules folder.

item.title: Salary: exploring Canadian salary guides and wage data
item.description:
Salary

Data analysisAPIDocker
PythonpandasPolarsPyPDF2JupyterFastAPIBeautifulSouppre-commit

Salary is an AlgoÉTS data project about pay in Canada. It turns recruitment-firm salary guides (PDF) and federal wage tables (CSV) into data frames, then compares jobs across provinces, regions and experience levels. It is useful to anyone who wants to see how a job such as cloud architect is paid from one region to another, and to readers interested in extracting tables from PDF reports.

SimilityVectorEmbedding is a set of Jupyter notebooks that turn a movie catalog into embeddings and look for similar films with several storage and ranking approaches. WearBlender

Blender scenes

WearBlender is a set of Blender scenes, published under ETSim, for learning and teaching how artists usually fake wear: worn edges, scratches, rotated normal maps, painted marks and proximity effects. It sits beside the ÉTS master’s research on wear in texture space, where wear comes from simulated contact rather than hand-built masks.

Overview

The repository holds only .blend files, a README and an MIT licence. The README lists five themes. The node types stored in each file show how the scenes cover them:

item.title: WearMachine: CAD files for a GelSight wear bench
item.description:
WearMachine

Hardware / CAD
STEPSTLDXFInkscape SVG

WearMachine collects the parts of the abrasion bench used in the ÉTS master’s research on wear in texture space: a sample slides on a rail under a chosen load, then is scanned with a GelSight sensor. The repository, published under ETSim, is for anyone who wants to rebuild or adapt the rig to evaluate wear, study friction or check simulations against measurements.

Overview

The README states the goal and the components: a GelSight bench, custom fixtures (the CAD files in the repository), load sensors, linear actuators and a control and acquisition system. Only the fixtures are in the repository. They are organised in three part families, each available in up to four formats:

item.title: WearSurfacesDatasets: measured wear-surface sequences
item.description:
WearSurfacesDatasets

DatasetAPI
PythonParquetWebDatasetGit LFSOpenCVFastAPIWebGPU

WearSurfacesDatasets publishes the surface textures captured during controlled wear tests, organised by material, abrasive grit, load and sliding distance. It is the public dataset of the ÉTS master’s research on wear in texture space, where it serves to compare simulated wear patterns with measured microgeometry, and it is published under ETSim for graphics and tribology researchers who need real wear progressions.

item.title: WearTrailsExperiments: contact-driven wear trails in the browser
item.description:
WearTrailsExperiments

Web experiments
JavaScriptthree.jsAmmo.jsWebGLglTF / GLB

WearTrailsExperiments gathers browser prototypes that turn the contact between a sliding body and the ground into persistent wear and flow maps. They explore, in JavaScript, the idea behind the ÉTS master’s research on wear in texture space: contact patches, tangential velocity and traction written into a texture where contact actually happened. The repository is published under ETSim for graphics researchers who want to try those ideas without building a native simulator.

item.title: BatchBacktesting: comparable strategy runs
item.description:
BatchBacktesting

BatchBacktesting turns a backtest into a repeatable batch: choose instruments, obtain and clean prices, run a strategy, and save comparable results. It is an AlgoÉTS repository; the facts below come from its source files and README as read for the companion article.

Overview

Why it exists. A batch backtest is a small data pipeline, and the project keeps every step visible in Python instead of behind a dashboard.

Best fit. Comparing one strategy across many instruments with the same recorded assumptions, then reading the per-instrument and aggregate CSVs side by side.

item.title: MistubaVideo
item.description:
MistubaVideo

MistubaVideo renders simulation exports with Mitsuba 3, under ETSim. The batch command processes OBJ sequences; the mitsuba-video helper reads recorded body poses and surface fields through manifest and TextureFriction source adapters. Facts below come from the repository documentation as read for the project introduction.

Overview

Why it exists. A simulation computes motion and surface change; rendering a recording shows where bodies moved and how material appearance evolved, and lets you change camera or lighting without repeating the simulation.

item.title: TrueMapData: height maps for metrology and graphics
item.description:
TrueMapData

TrueMapData is a Python library and tmd-process CLI for TrueMap and GelSight height maps, maintained under ETSim. It reads surface captures as NumPy arrays and provides analysis and graphics export. Facts below come from the repository README and guides as read for the companion article.

Overview

Why it exists. One surface representation that serves metrology work and graphics assets such as displacement maps or meshes.

Best fit. Inspecting measured surfaces, comparing captures over time (wear), and exporting normal maps, displacement maps or meshes with physical scale preserved.

item.title: Workshop1: Python learning notebooks
item.description:
Workshop1

Workshop1 is an AlgoÉTS notebook-based Python workshop. The sequence moves from setup through API calls, pandas and visualisation, and ends with an Apple-price EMA exercise. Facts below come from the repository as read for the companion article.

Overview

Why it exists. A beginner workshop where each new concept has somewhere to go: a request becomes a table, the table becomes a chart.

Best fit. First contact with Python for finance students, before moving to a batch experiment such as BatchBacktesting.

item.title: nova-backtest: Historical candles into a strategy simulation
item.description:
nova-backtest

Python libraryForkArchivedAlgorithm
PythonpandasNumPyPlotlyPoetrypytestSphinx

nova-backtest is a Python library for backtesting crypto trading strategies, published on PyPI as novalabs-backtest (version 1.1.10 in pyproject.toml). It downloads historical candles from Binance, Bybit, OKX, KuCoin, Huobi, MEXC, BTCEX and Oanda, runs a strategy over many pairs at once and reports statistics. This repository is an archived fork of the NovaLabs project; the commits made here in April 2023 rename the package directory and update the README. The interest of the code is how it simulates trades without a bar-by-bar loop.

item.description:
DasherControl

Another Interactive Configurable Dashboard with Customisable GridItem with IFrame and Bookmark and other cool features with basic Container Controller for Docker made with Vuejs and Rust (rocket).

Why …

Everything is a web app that can be installed with a docker in a container. I want to manage all my web applications on one dashboard like Sonarr and Jellyfin without opening like 10 tabs in chrome (rip my ram). When using services like Portainer or the Docker CLI, it’s long to set up a reverse proxy with SSL to secure your homelab. So I want to write widgets (Applets) that can do all my tasks that I do on the daily when managing my homelab. Also, I want to make a simple dashboard with widgets (vuejs component) like Windows Vista, but on the web and saved in a database.

item.title: RawAnalyser
item.description:
here

RawAnalyser

RawAnalyser is a Python tool for analyzing raw images: black and white clipping detection, gamma calculation, and flatness with vignette detection (Algolux).

Prerequisites

You need to have Python 2.7 installed and the following libraries:

  • json
  • time
  • numpy
  • scipy
  • pyqt5
  • argparse
  • argcomplete
  • watchdog
  • logging
  • colorama
  • plotly
  • matplotlib

Usage

  1. Run the RawAnalyser script:
python RawAnalyser.py <pathfolder> <pointfile> --func <clipping,gamma,vignette,histogram,noHist,basic, default all> --bl <black level, default 1024> --vignette <pathvignette>
  1. Start the GUI:
python GUI.py
  1. Check the value of the pixel and the color with the bayer pattern:
python RawPixel.pt input<file> x y --bitdepth <8,10,16,default 16>

Scripts Description

RawAnalyser.py

Checks black and white clipping levels in a raw image. Takes a folder path and a JSON file with the region of interest and gray patches.
